raw_response:
I’m still doing the wheat-maize rotation on all 2.6 mu. My land is small, so I can’t gamble too much. What I do is mostly based on what has worked on my own field and what other people around here do. Last year, wheat still responded when I put a bit of nitrogen at jointing, and maize did better when I didn’t delay sowing after wheat harvest. Water from the well helps, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate too many times unless the crop really needs it. I have some off-farm work in the family, so I also need a plan that is steady and manageable, not something too complicated.

For wheat, I’ll sow in early October with a local improved variety that people in the village commonly use. I’ll give base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once around jointing if the stand looks a little weak or yellow. I’ll irrigate mainly at sowing or before winter if the soil is dry, then around jointing and grain filling if needed. For maize, I’ll plant as soon as the wheat comes off, no dragging it out, because every day counts in this system. I’ll use hybrid seed, do light tillage or direct sow after wheat if I can arrange it, and put most attention on getting the seedlings established fast. I’ll fertilize in two parts again, but I won’t push inputs too hard because on 2.6 mu I need to watch cash first.
